# 1 Enoch Chapter 13 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 13 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 13:1 — Address to Azazel: quotation style

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | Single-quotes, second-person formal ('thou') | Preserves archaic address |
| LOGOS | Single-quotes, second-person modern ('you') | Modern formal |
| PNEUMA | Double-quotes, second-person modern | Direct speech with modern punctuation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted single-quotes with modern 'you' (LOGOS). The archaic 'thou' (EMET) is inconsistent with the project's general conventions. Double-quotes (PNEUMA) are acceptable but single-quotes are preferred for direct speech of divine pronouncements in this project's style.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS convention.

---

## 13:5 — 'could not speak with Him' — reason for inability

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "for-shame of-their-sins for-which-they-had-been-condemned" | Preserves the causal chain literally |
| LOGOS | "for shame of their sins for which they had been condemned" | Same; more readable |
| PNEUMA | "because they were so ashamed of the sins that had brought judgment upon them" | Expands and paraphrases the causal chain |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. PNEUMA's expansion is clear but adds 'judgment' as an interpolation where the Ge'ez says 'condemnation' (which LOGOS preserves as 'condemned'). The literal rendering is more precise.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 13:7 — Place name: 'Abelsjail' vs. 'Abel-mayin'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Abelsjail" | Follows Charles 1906 edition transliteration |
| LOGOS | "Abel-mayin" | Follows Knibb/Nickelsburg edition; means 'meadow of waters' |
| PNEUMA | "Abel-mayin" | Agrees with LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'Abel-mayin' (LOGOS/PNEUMA). The Knibb edition's transliteration is the modern scholarly standard and the place name meaning ('meadow of waters') fits the context of 'waters of Dan.' EMET's 'Abelsjail' follows the outdated Charles edition.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 13:8 — 'visions of chastisement' vs. 'visions of wrath'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "visions of-chastisement" | The Ge'ez term can mean punishment/discipline |
| LOGOS | "visions of wrath" | Captures the divine anger dimension more forcefully |
| PNEUMA | "visions of judgment" | Dynamic; 'judgment' is the functional outcome |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'visions of wrath' (LOGOS). The Ge'ez term in this context refers to the divine anger at sin rather than remedial discipline ('chastisement'). 'Judgment' (PNEUMA) is accurate in outcome but loses the affective dimension of divine anger.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## Overall assessment

Chapter 13 is a pivotal narrative chapter containing several significant textual decisions: the place names (Abelsjail vs. Abel-mayin), the theological nuance of the Watchers' inability to face God (v. 5), and the nature of the vision received (v. 8). Total significant divergences: 4.
